blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Cyclic homology and cohomology were independently discovered by Alain Connes [@connes0] and Boris Tsygan [@tsygan] in the early 1980's, and should be thought of as extensions of de Rham (co)homology to various categories of noncommutative algebras. Quantum groups also appeared in the same period, with the first example of a "compact quantum group" in the C\*-algebraic setting being Woronowicz's "quantum $SU(2)$" [@wo_suq2].

blocks.title: Covariant differential calculi
blocks.content:
[]{#section_diff_calc_suq2 label="section_diff_calc_suq2"}

In this section we identify the classes in twisted cyclic cohomology of $\mathcal{A}(SL_q(2))$ of the twisted cyclic cocycles arising from the three and four dimensional covariant differential calculi originally discovered for quantum $SU(2)$ by Woronowicz.

blocks.title: three dimensional left-covariant calculus
blocks.content:
[]{#section:3dcalculus label="section:3dcalculus"}

The automorphism of $\mathcal{A}(SL_q (2))$ corresponding to Woronowicz's three-dimensional left-covariant calculus over quantum $SU(2)$ is $$\label{3dcalc_aut}
\sigma(a) = q^{-2} a, \quad
\sigma(b) = q^4 b, \quad
\sigma(c) = q^{-4} c,\quad
\sigma(d) = q^2 d$$ The twisted cyclic 3-cocycle over $\mathcal{A}(SL_q (2))$ arising from this calculus was written down in [@sw1] section 3 (denoted by $\tau_{\omega,h}$) and [@kmt] section 5 (corresponding to the linear functional $\int$).

[]{#section:4dcalculus label="section:4dcalculus"}

blocks.title: Conclusions
blocks.content:
[]{#conclusions label="conclusions"}

The original motivation for this work was the belief that calculating twisted cyclic cohomology would give new insight into existing classification results [@istvan; @hs] for covariant differential calculi over quantum $SL(2)$ and quantum $SU(2)$.
